Laurent — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Recap (what we agreed)
- BrightPath will validate a local dev run of Redwood inference (dev/dev sandbox) using our starter kit.
- Focus areas for the quick test: auth + token exchange, request routing to a dev model, embeddings inference and a simple reranker, and a structured-output example with a tool call stub.
- Security note: you flagged interest in private endpoint options (VPC peering) — we’ll surface those after you're comfortable with the local flow.

Immediate next steps (owners & timelines)
1) Kimberly/Redwood: share starter-kit bundle + minimal auth sample (today) — attached.
2) BrightPath: run the local dev kit on a laptop or dev VM, try the Python quickstart and the TypeScript example, report any env-related blockers (by EOD Monday).
3) Karthik/Redwood: prepare a 30-min tech-check (remote screenshare) after BrightPath hits the smoke test (propose Tue 10:00am PT).

Starter kit contents attached: brightpath-starterkit-v1.tar.gz (contains python/ts samples, Dockerfile, docker-compose, README), auth-config-sample.yaml.

Common env checklist (short)
- REDWOOD_API_KEY or local token file (see auth-config-sample.yaml)
- REDWOOD_ENDPOINT (default: http://localhost:8080 for local runtime)
- NODE_ENV=development (TS sample) / PYENV virtualenv active
- Docker available for containerized run (optional)

If you hit anything environmental (CORS, firewall, local port conflicts), paste logs into the HubSpot ticket linked below and we’ll triage in the tech-check.

HubSpot ticket: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/67890

Thanks — Kim

Laurent / Kim — quick technical supplement below with minimal commands and a small TypeScript example for the structured output/tool-call pattern. This should be enough to run locally without secrets being exposed.

Local Docker Compose (minimal)
- docker-compose.yml (in starter kit) spins up:
  - local-proxy (listens on :8080, forwards to local runtime mock)
  - sample-client (optional, curls the endpoint)

Python smoke test (local, venv)
1) tar xzf brightpath-starterkit-v1.tar.gz && cd brightpath-starterkit/python
2) python -m venv .env && source .env/bin/activate
3) pip install -r requirements.txt
4) export REDWOOD_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:8080
5) export REDWOOD_API_KEY=local_test_token_eyJ... (use the token in auth-config-sample.yaml)
6) python examples/embeddings_and_rerank_smoke.py

Key Python pattern (pseudo)
- POST /v1/embeddings -> returns vectors; store locally then call /v1/rerank with query + candidate vectors (see examples/.)

TypeScript structured-output + tool-call (minimal)
- File: typescript/structured-tool-call.ts (in repo)
- Run: cd typescript && npm install && export REDWOOD_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:8080 && export REDWOOD_API_KEY=local_test_token && node structured-tool-call.js

Example structured output payload (what our TS sample demonstrates)
{
  "input": "Summarize patient note and call medication-check tool if reminders needed.",
  "format": { "type": "json_schema", "schema": { "action": { "type": "string" }, "reminder": { "type": "boolean" } } }
}

The sample client will parse that JSON and, in the tool-call stub, emit a POST to /internal-tools/medication-check (local mock).

Auth notes (short)
- Starter kit uses a non-rotating dev token in auth-config-sample.yaml for convenience. For any persistent or sensitive data runs, use short-lived tokens (we can demo a token-exchange flow) or mount a credentials file with restricted perms.

Routing & batching tips
- For local testing keep sequence lengths short (<512 tokens) to avoid long synthetic latencies.
- If you want to exercise batching behavior, our Docker compose includes a small load-generator (samples/loadgen.py) that will show throughput/latency tradeoffs. Ben can join the tech-check to explain batching knobs (max_batch_size, max_wait_ms).

If you want, I can paste the minimal docker-compose.yml and the TypeScript snippet into the Drive folder right now. Otherwise I’ll bring them to the tech-check.

—Karthik
Director, Developer Platform (serving runtime)
